summary: Not as a dip-buying or breakdown signal. On BTC, ETH and SOL, crossing up the lower band, closing below it, or shorting a cross down through it did no better than random candles on 1h, 4h or daily. What held is on the upper band: on 1h, price above it was 0.36% further up than after random candles 20 candles later, but these entries cluster in volatile candles of a window that rose, so price moved more after them rather than picking direction.

verdicts.use: Riding price above the upper band
verdicts.text: Price moved more than after random candles on 1h, 4h and daily, in a window that rose. These entries fire in volatile stretches, so this reflects when they fire, not a call on direction, and on 4h and daily it came from uptrends.

verdicts.use: Buying the breakout (cross up the upper band)
verdicts.text: On 1h, no better than random. On 4h and daily price moved more after the cross, in uptrends only and in a window that rose, so it reflects the volatile candles it fires on rather than direction.

verdicts.use: Buying the dip at the lower band
verdicts.text: No better than random entries on 1h, 4h or daily, as a cross back up through the lower band or as a close below it, with either range length.

verdicts.use: Shorting a break below the lower band
verdicts.text: No better than random entries on 1h, 4h or daily, pooled and in both uptrends and downtrends.

notes: On 4h, price crossing up the lower band gave 721 entries in 362 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.64% behind random entries, inside the luck band. With Range length 20 the cross lands in the same place, 0.44% behind. Closes below the lower band show nothing on 1h, 4h or daily either.

On 1h, price above the upper band gave 10,236 entries in 1,532 moves. Twenty candles later price was 0.36% further up than after random candles. That holds without its strongest stretch, at 10, 50 and 100 candles, and in uptrends. In downtrends it beat random by 0.29%, but only because of signals on May 8–9, 2025; without them, chance. The entries cluster in volatile candles, so in a window that rose they beat random longs because of when they fire, not because they pick direction.

On 4h, the same level beat random by 1.16% and the cross up through the upper band by 0.77%, but neither shows at 50 candles. Both come from uptrends: above the 200-day SMA the cross beat random by 0.93%, below it it showed nothing, and the level showed nothing there too. On 1h the cross landed at the top of the luck band, at 0.19%. On daily the gaps reach 8%, but in uptrends they vanish without the stretch that starts on Jul 31, 2021, and downtrends have too few episodes to judge. Here too, price moved more after volatile candles in a rising window.

Single stretches can fake a result. On ETH 4h, crossing up the lower band looked 1.19% worse than random, and closes below it 1.23% worse. Each rests on one stretch: signals on May 16–20, 2021, around the May 2021 crash, and on Jun 10–18, 2022. The June stretch also drives the 4h downtrend result for closes below the lower band, 0.82% behind random and chance without it. The ETH short on a cross down the lower band looked 1.25% better, again only from May 16–19, 2021.

For a long DCA bot, the lower band adds no timing on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit carry the result. A short bot that opens on a break below the lower band gets nothing from it. Price above the upper band on 1h or 4h is a filter to test beside other conditions while the pair is in an uptrend. Price moved more after those candles, so set the take profit and DCA steps for larger moves. In downtrends the 4h filter showed nothing, which is a reason to leave it out there.
